etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From いつ (itsu, “when”) + も (mo, “even, also”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Derived from 貧しい (mazushii, “poor”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Compound of 一昨 (issaku-, “the previous... before...”) + 日 (jitsu, “day”).
First cited to a text from 1275.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/wotot͡sufi/ → /wototofi/ → /wototowi/ → /ototoi/
First cited to a text from roughly 953.
Shift from Old Japanese ototsui (see Etymology 3 below).
The kanji spelling is from issakujitsu (see Etymology 1 above).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨woto₂ tu pi₁⟩ → */wotətupʲi/ → /wotot͡sufi/ → /otot͡suwi/ → /otot͡sui/
First attested in the Man'yōshū (c. 759 CE).
Originally a compound of 遠 (oto, “distant, distant past”) + つ (tsu, Old Japanese case-marker particle) + 日 (hi, “day”).
The kanji spelling is from issakujitsu (see Etymology 1 above).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 付(つ)き合(あ)う (tsukiau, “keep company with; get along with”), equivalent to 付(つ)き (tsuki) + 合(あ)い (ai).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 切(き)る (kiru, “to cut”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 切(き)り (kiri) above. The kiri changes to giri as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 版行 (hankō) > hanko.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 劣る (oto₂ru), from Proto-Japonic *ətəru, from Proto-Japonic *ət-.
Via Old Japanese root ot-, cognate with 落(お)ちる (ochiru, “to fall”, intransitive) and 落(お)とす (otosu, “to drop something”, transitive).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 勇(いさ)む (isamu) + しい (-shii)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 大(たい) (tai, “big, large”) + 戦(せん) (sen, “battle”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE in sense 1.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 實 (MC zyit).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. Thought to be originally a compound of 真 (sa, “_([term?])”) + 根 (ne, “root of a plant”).
First appears in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE in sense 2.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the verb 実(みの)る (minoru, “to bear fruit”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 当つ (atu), following 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Derived from 悔いる (kuiru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/satu/ → /sat͡su/
From Middle Chinese 札 (MC tsreat).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/pumi ita/ → /ɸumita/ → /ɸunda/ → /ɸuda/
Originally a compound of 文(ふみ) (fumi, “writing”) + 板(いた) (ita, “board, plank”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 武器 (MC mjuX khijH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 消防(しょうぼう) (shōbō, “fire fighting”) + 署(しょ) (-sho, “station, office”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 片付(かたづ)ける (katazukeru, “to tidy up”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 率 (MC lwit).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) of verb 盛る (sakaru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) of verb 盛る (moru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 研究(けんきゅう) (kenkyū, “research”) + 室(しつ) (-shitsu, “room”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 量(はか)る (hakaru).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with Japanese 写る.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨i₁ne⟩ → /ine/
From Old Japanese. Attested in the Man'yōshū of circa 759 CE. In turn, from Proto-Japonic *inay.
Possibly related to 米 (yone, “rice (husked grains of the Asian rice plant, Oryza sativa)”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese.
Commonly found in compounds, rarely in isolation.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: /kumiahi/: *[kumiapi] → [kumiaɸi] → [kumiawi] → [kumiai].

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/fada aka/ → /fadaka/ → /hadaka/
Originally a compound of 肌 (hada, “skin”) + 赤 (aka, “red”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/djuːeu/ → /d͡ʑuːeu/ → /d͡ʑuːjoː/
From Middle Chinese compound 重要 (drjowng^X ʔjiewᴴ, literally “heavy + important”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Specialization of 皮(かわ) (kawa, “skin”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 食(た)べ (tabe, “eating”, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 食(た)べる (taberu, “to eat”)) + 物(もの) (-mono, “thing”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Contraction of 高(こう)等(とう)学(がっ)校(こう) (kōtō-gakkō, “high school”).
